title: Runtime allocator leak and fragmentation recovery for multi-tenant GPU OOM escalations
creator: Arielle Gomez
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported recurrent GPU OOMs during sustained inference workloads. Investigations showed a noise pattern: memory pressure rose slowly across long-lived workers and then triggered OOMs unpredictably. This ticket tracks triage, short-term mitigations, the runtime patch (allocator + KV cache guardrails), and rollout for all deployment modes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start long-lived dedicated worker with mixed seq-len traffic (1% large sequences > 4k tokens).
2) Enable KV cache with per-request pinning and model quantization flags (int8 fused kernels).
3) Send synthetic sustained traffic for 12+ hours that exercises attention cache eviction patterns.
4) Observe GPU memory usage slowly climb with fragmentation spikes preceding OOMs; reproduces on both hosted multitenant and private single-tenant setups.
mitigation_actions: - Disable KV cache pinning by default for affected model families on Hosted (hotfix rollout 2025-02-19).
- Add autoscale policy to spawn replacement workers proactively for Dedicated customers experiencing memory creep.
- Provide Private deployment playbook to throttle long sequence traffic and enable temporary restart cron for affected pods.
root_cause_summary: A combination of an allocator interaction with persistent KV cache allocations and deferred free patterns caused GPU memory to become fragmented over time. The runtime's small-allocation path didn’t coalesce freed regions due to a heuristic mismatch introduced in the int8 kernel integration; long-lived pinned KV tensors prevented contiguous large buffers from being allocated, causing OOMs when large sequences required contiguous scratch space.
fix_summary: Patch runtime allocator to expose periodic coalescing and add a low-overhead compaction pass opportunistically between requests. Harden KV cache lifecycle: introduce a soft-cap per-worker, eviction callback to unpin stale KV slices, and defensive checks to reject new pin requests when fragmentation thresholds are exceeded. Add telemetry emitting fragmentation metrics and a new SLO alert rule.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Hotfix - Hosted): rollback KV pinning and deploy allocator guard (2025-02-19) — completed for high-traffic tenants.
Phase 1 (Canary - Dedicated): deploy allocator+KV guard to 10% of Dedicated pools with metric-driven canary window (2025-02-22) — monitoring in progress.
Phase 2 (Private): publish patch bundle and upgrade guide; offer assisted upgrade for customers with high fragmentation (target 2025-03-10).
Phase 3 (Full Rollout): auto-enable improvements and alert updates across all clusters after 48h of stable canary metrics.
prs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 - allocator: add coalescing pass and fragmentation metric
github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4326 - kvcache: add soft-cap, eviction callback, and defensive pin rejection
github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/119 - hosted-config: temporary disable kv pinning for affected models
postmortem_actions: 1) Instrument per-worker fragmentation and peak contiguous allocation metrics and retain for 30d.
2) Add regression tests that simulate long-lived KV-heavy workloads with random large sequence injections.
3) Improve release checklist to include allocator kernel compatibility tests for quantized/integer kernels.
4) Document safe KV cache configuration for Private deployments and include an automated health-check script.
customer_communication: 2025-02-19: Outbound email to affected Hosted customers: temporary mitigation applied and engineering investigating root cause.
2025-02-24: Dedicated customers in canary received a release note and opt-in instructions; account teams notified for high-risk tenants.
2025-03-03: Draft of public postmortem and customer-facing summary being reviewed.
